thread:
maria: Heads-up — saw a steady VRAM growth on longctx runs with paged KV when switching between MI250 and A100 stacks. Repro script attached. :eyes:
oli: details? what workload, batch size, model?
sam: which kernel path? is this the tiled paged-attn or the contiguous fallback?
maria: tiled paged-attn. model=redwood/longctx-mix, seq=32k, batch=1, batching disabled. Happens after ~1.2M tokens, memory climbs ~200MB every minute until OOM on MI250. Not repro on A100 in same infra.
jin: can you paste the repro command and the pagetable stats?
maria: sure — run.sh:
```
./run_infer.sh --model redwood/longctx-mix --seq 32768 --tokens 1500000 --disable-batching --kv-pager=on --coalesce=auto
```
paged stats (snippet):
```
PAGETABLE: entries=1.2M, free_holes=12, shadow_hash_hits=84%
EVICT_METRICS: eviction_cycles=230k, last_handoff=246ms
```
oli: curious about "shadow_hash_hits" — our MI250 kernel has a different page key hashing (tiling->stripe) than NVIDIA; possible collision causing reuse miss and new allocations.
sam: also check kernel selection: on MI250 we pick scalar-copy kernel for kv->page merges, on A100 we use vectorized coalesce. That could change order and fragmentation.
perf-bot: perf trace uploaded: https://perf-collector/internal/trace/1739012345 (sampled counters: l2-cache-miss 2.1%, smem-usage 78%)
andrew: I dug into trace — on MI250 we see repeated small evictions (~4k pages) triggered by a stale owner check failing, then immediate partial refills. On A100 the same sequence is amortized via batched refills.
tess: can we try forcing the vector coalesce kernel on MI250 to confirm? maybe kernel selection heuristic is too conservative due to assumed alignment.
maria: good idea — I forced coalesce via env var KERNEL_FORCE=vector and reran for 200k tokens: memory plateaued, no leak.
jin: wow, that nails it. So it's not pagetable metadata corruption, it's allocation/eviction ordering + kernel path exposing fragmentation growth.
oli: next question: why does our MI250 scalar path cause more fragmentation vs A100 scalar? could be different PCIe NV-link buffer pressure and smaller DMA burst sizes. Need microbench.
sam: I pushed a small test patch that changes the handoff heuristic threshold from 32->16 pages for MI250; CI run queued. If that reduces churn we can ship a soft-fallback.
alexa: note: we also saw slowdowns when kernel reverted to fallback on large seqs — add telemetry to Console to surface "kv_kernel_selected" per request so users see this.
maria: agreed — add telemetry + an alert when kernel != preferred for >1% requests. That will help correlate client-side regressions.
deploy-bot: canary build 2026.03.15-kv-fix started on staging (ami=kv-handoff-20260315).
andrew: two actionable items: (1) add telemetry + opt-in force-vector for MI250 in debug builds, (2) tune handoff threshold and test cross-arch. I'll own (2).
tess: I'll take (1) and add dashboard widgets showing kernel selection, evict-rate, shadow-hash-hit.
maria: thanks all. Follow-up: I'll open a tracking issue with the perf traces, the forced run logs, and the forced-kernel evidence. If we see anything that smells like metadata corruption we escalate, but right now it looks like fragmentation-amplified-by-kernel-path. :thumbsup:
oli: add a note to the PR to mention we observed different DMA burst behavior on MI250 which may alter coalescing assumptions.
sam: fwiw, also test with KV cache prefix caching enabled — that changed reuse pattern on A100 and might reduce churn on MI250 too.
maria: good call, I'll add that variant to the repro matrix.
jin: ping me when you have the dashboard — I'll watch overnight runs.
maria: will do. Thanks everyone.
